verdict.rationale: Smithery documents a dedicated server page for discovering and trying each listed server. It scans server metadata, with a static server-card fallback, and it captures tool schemas (a typed SDK is generated from them). It also distinguishes local stdio (MCPB bundle) from URL-hosted servers, and it remains a public registry after the hosted-service shutdown. However, no evidence shows that tools, input schemas, transport or hosting attributes are actually displayed for inspection before connecting; the CLI's `tool get` works on an existing connection. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that server pages expose per-tool input schemas, transport type and hosting attributes before connecting, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of that pre-connection inspection view.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect a listed server's tools, input schemas, transport, and hosting attributes before connecting to it

citations.quote: Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
you can provide server metadata manually via a static server card at `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`
For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
Every MCP server published on Smithery gets a typed TypeScript SDK generated from its tool and trigger schemas.
